disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending, Source Conflict and BLOCKED. Official NVIDIA documentation separates NVENC encoding, NVDEC decoding and display rendering; it also requires querying the selected device's codec capabilities. FFmpeg separately documents software `libaom-av1` and NVIDIA NVENC encoders. These authorities can define a safe future evidence structure, but cannot choose whether this project row owns encode, decode/display or both, which exact GPU is in scope, or what output/quality/visual result is authoritative. decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1783, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, Round-2 UNRESOLVED result, pending/conflict/blocked analyses, ED-01 through ED-30 and official NVIDIA/FFmpeg documentation were read. The next formal identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1784 / Wistron-HW-00417-V002 / d07fd08d1a99b05c.

NVIDIA's NVENC guide defines encoding as consuming raw YUV/RGB frames and producing a compliant AV1 bitstream, with supported encoder GUIDs queried from the selected device. A null-output software run does not provide that hardware or retained-bitstream evidence.

NVIDIA's NVDEC guide defines AV1 decoding as a separate path that yields decoded frames; displaying those frames requires an additional graphics conversion/rendering path. Therefore encoding, decoding and physical display cannot share an inferred PASS.

FFmpeg documents `libaom-av1` as a separate encoder from NVENC encoders. The DeepSeek proposal neither binds `av1_nvenc`/NVENC capability nor prevents software fallback and it discards output with the null muxer.

Exact AV1 encode/decode support is GPU-architecture and capability dependent. A GPU that can decode AV1 does not thereby prove AV1 NVENC encode support, so exact GPU UUID/BDF and per-device capability evidence are mandatory.

The owner must select stage ownership and define profile/level, bit depth/chroma/pixel format, resolution/frame rate, duration/frame count, GOP/rate control/quality, deterministic input, retained output/container/bitstream, decode reference and the visual oracle/path if display remains in scope.

The 1-minute Machine Time is scheduling metadata, not an approved media duration, frame count or acceptance threshold. No media command, GPU workload, scratch write, playback, display inspection, log clear or DUT action was executed.
